function: Learned joint transmit beamforming for ISAC: communication and sensing beamforming matrices minimizing the sensing beampattern MSE under communication SINR constraints (p. 4).
system: BS with ULA of M=10 half-wavelength antennas; L=2 users with channel vector hl, K=3 radar targets; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 2-3, 10).
method: GNN with FCNN encoders and message passing, then an implicit projection solving a convex program; trained without labels on sensing MSE plus a ReLU barrier (pp. 4-8).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rayleigh fading with large-scale factor 10^-3 d^-2.67, users i.i.d. in a rectangular region, ULA array response; 10000 training, 1000 validation, 1000 test samples (p. 10).
test_conditions: Train with L=2 users, K=3 targets, 10000 samples; test on 1000 samples, and on 3-6 users without retraining (Fig. 9); retrained for each SINR threshold (pp. 10-12).
baselines: SDR [33] and ZF [33] optimization; fully connected DNN with four layers of 512 neurons; GNN without projection as ablation (pp. 10, 12).
metrics: Sensing beampattern MSE, beampattern plots, SINR constraint satisfaction ratio, average computation time (Figs. 6-11, Tables II-III) (pp. 10-13).
complexity: Orders of complexity of GNN and projection modules (p. 9); 0.0002 s per inference versus 4.87 s (ZF) and 6.97 s (SDR) at N=180 (Table II, p. 12).
q1_support: p. 10: "The channel between the BS and user l is modeled as Rayleigh fading" with a path-loss factor 10^-3 d^-2.67; a custom simulator, and the paper never mentions 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured channels.
q2_support: p. 11: "we train a GNN module on the dataset with L = 2, and then directly apply it to a multi-user scenario"; Fig. 9 (p. 11) tests 3 to 6 users with the weights copied and no retraining.
q3_support: p. 10: "Benchmark 1 is the SDR based optimization algorithm proposed in [33]."; p. 10: "Benchmark 3 is the deep neural network (DNN) based algorithm. We design a conventional FCNN for comparison."; p. 11: "Fig. 8 shows that the proposed GNN-IP algorithm achieves better sensing performance than the DNN algorithm and ZF optimization algorithm."
q4_support: p. 9: "the overall computation complexity of the GNN module in the inference stage" is given as an order, and the projection module as O((LM)^4.5 log(1/epsilon)); p. 12: Tables II and III list the average computation time (0.0002 s for GNN-IP versus 6.9714 s for SDR at N=180).
q5_support: p. 10: "The sizes of the training, validation, and test sets are fixed as 10000, 1000, and 1000, respectively." The data are the paper's own simulated channels, and the paper gives no repository, DOI or data statement.
notes: Included in area 5: the learned method designs the joint communication and sensing beamformers of an ISAC base station, and beamforming in an ISAC system is area 5. Tables I to III were not in the extracted text, so they were read from the page images of pp. 10 and 12. Points for the reviewer: (1) the output of the GNN is passed through a projection module that solves a convex program (CVX, SOCP) when the constraints are violated (pp. 7-9, Algorithm 1 on p. 9); the learned element is the GNN, and the projection is used for 0% of samples up to 8 dB and 3.2% at 9 dB (Table III, p. 12). (2) q2 rests on the scalability test of Fig. 9 (trained with L = 2, applied to 3 to 6 users); the paper also says the GNN must be retrained when the SINR constraint changes (p. 12: "needs to be retrained"), and the dynamic scenario of Fig. 8 only moves each user by at most 1 m along x and 2 m along y per time slot (p. 11), which is not counted as a new condition. (3) q3 rests on the fully connected DNN benchmark, a standard architecture applied to the same problem; the GNN without projection is an ablation and is not counted. (4) The carrier frequency is not stated.
